ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r11.claim: ضنك means narrowness and hardship, and الضناك can describe a fleshy woman.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r1.claim: Turning away from God’s reminder, meaning the Qur’an or other revealed books, brings a constricted, difficult life; ḍank is an invariant adjective for hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r1.anchor: والذكر يقع على القرآن وعلى سائر الكتب الإلهية. وضنك: مصدر يوصف به المذكر والمؤنث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r2.claim: A line by Antara illustrates a constricted dwelling as a source of hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r2.anchor: ومنه قول عنترة: إن المنية لو تمثل مثلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi and refers to the grave squeezing the ribs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: نزلت هذه الآية في الأسود بن عبد الأسد المخزومي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r4.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and al-Kalbi interpret the constricted life as the narrow life of Hell, where food and drink are torment and inhabitants neither die nor live.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة والكلبي: هو الضيق في الآخرة في جهنم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r5.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r5.claim: Ata says a disbeliever’s life is constricted because he lacks certainty about reward and punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء: المعيشة الضنك معيشة الكافر لأنه غير موقن بالثواب والعقاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r6.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets the hardship as loss of contentment, leaving a person perpetually unsatisfied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: يسلب القناعة حتى لا يشبع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r7.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri and al-Suddi identify it as grave punishment; Abu Hurayra transmits this interpretation from the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r7.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري والسدي: هو عذاب القبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r8.speaker: الجوهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r8.claim: Al-Jawhari places the hardship in worldly life: even a wealthy unbeliever is distressed by greed, ambition, worldly troubles, and lack of ease.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r8.anchor: وقال الجوهري: المعيشة الضنك في الدنيا، والمعنى أن الكافر وإن كان متسع الحال والمال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r9.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r9.claim: Another group says the constricted livelihood comes from eating unlawful food.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r12.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r12.claim: Hasan reads ḍankī with feminine alif, no tanwin, and imāla; the majority read ḍankan with tanwin and an inflected final vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p393/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ضنكي بألف التأنيث ولا تنوين وبالإمالة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r4.claim: The expression maʿīshatan ḍankan denotes a life without peace of mind or inner satisfaction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r4.anchor: refers to a life devoid of peace of mind and inner satisfaction

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r5.claim: Only faith in God fills the human inner vacuum; worldly resources offer temporary joy but cannot relieve spiritual anxiety, while true firm faith brings satisfaction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p80/r5.anchor: Similar is the case with a human being.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r1.claim: The discussion concerns people with true faith, not everyone who merely claims faith; outwardly comfortable unbelievers may conceal inner threats, doubts, and fears.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r1.anchor: the discussion is not with those who merely lay claim to faith but with those who have true faith

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r2.claim: Hidden spiritual distress may be visible only to the person or to people with faith-based insight, despite an appearance of happiness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r2.anchor: Only they themselves can see them or those who have the insight of faith in them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r3.claim: God's remembrance clears the faculties of sight, hearing, and intellect; those who evade it are spiritually blind, deaf, and intellectually deprived despite possessing these faculties.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r3.anchor: removes hurdles from the faculties of sight, hearing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r4.claim: Human faculties were given to recognize the signs throughout creation, not to become enslaved to what is merely tangible; failing to perceive the obvious leaves a person understanding nothing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r4.anchor: These favours were not given to people so that they become slaves of what is palpable and tangible

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r1.claim: ضنكا is an adjective of معيشة derived from a verbal noun; it stays unchanged for singular, dual, and plural.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r1.anchor: وأصله المصدر فلذلك لم يؤنث. ويقع للمفرد والمثنى والمجموع بلفظ واحد.

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r2.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r2.claim: The general reading has ضنكا with tanwin in connected recitation and its replacement by alif at pause, like other declinable forms.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور " ضنكا " بالتنوين وصلا وإبداله ألفا وقفا كسائر المعربات.

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r3.speaker: فرقة
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r3.claim: A group reads ضنكى; the alif may replace tanwin with connected reading treated like pause, or be the feminine alif in a verbal noun formed on فعلى.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r3.anchor: وقرأت فرقة قوله: " ضنكى " بألف كسكرى. وفي هذه الألف احتمالان،

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r4.claim: ضنك means constriction and hardship; the derived phrase ضنك عيشه describes a straitened life.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r4.anchor: وامرأة ضناك كثيرة لحم البدن، كأنهم تخيلوا ضيق جلدها به.

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r5.claim: The expression امرأة ضناك means a woman with much flesh, imagined as skin constricted by it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r5.anchor: وامرأة ضناك كثيرة لحم البدن، كأنهم تخيلوا ضيق جلدها به.

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r6.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r6.claim: The general reading uses first-person نون and an indicative verb as a new sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r6.anchor: وقرأ العامة " ونحشره " بالنون ورفع الفعل على الاستئناف.

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r7.speaker: أبان ابن تغلب
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r7.claim: Aban ibn Taghlib and others pause the rā; this can be jussive coordination with the conditional apodosis or a lightening of the indicative form.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبان ابن تغلب في آخرين بتسكين الراء. وهي محتملة لوجهين،

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r8.speaker: فرقة
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r8.claim: A group reads in the third person, with the understood subject either God or the angel.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r8.anchor: بياء الغيبة وهو الله تعالى أو الملك.

SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r9.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r9.claim: In another narration Aban ibn Taghlib reads ونحشره with a vowelless hā while connected; the author relates this to the languages of Banu Aqil and Banu Kilab or to treating connection like pause.
SAMIN-DURR:20:124/r9.anchor: بسكون الهاء وصلا. وتخريجها: إما على لغة بني عقيل وبني كلاب،

ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r1.claim: ضنك literally means narrowness and hardship; Zajjaj thinks the constricted life here is in Hell.
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r1.anchor: الضنك: أصله في اللغة الضيق والشدة، ومعناه - والله أعلم - أن هذه المعيشة الضنك

ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r2.speaker: أكثر التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r2.claim: Most exegetical reports identify the constricted life as punishment in the grave, rather than Zajjaj's preferred interpretation of life in Hell.
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r2.anchor: وأكثر ما جاء في التفسير أنه عذاب القبر.

ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r3.claim: The resurrection as blind parallels the description of criminals as blue-eyed in 20:102.
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r3.anchor: وقوله: (ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى). مثل ونحشر المجرمين يومئذ زرقا،

ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r4.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r4.claim: Another explanation is that he is blind to his proof: he has no argument by which to find guidance, rather than possessing a proof he cannot see.
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r4.anchor: وقيل أعمى عن حجته، وتأويله أنه لا حجة له يهتدي إليها، لا أن له حجة،

ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r5.claim: People have no claim against God after the messengers; God has the decisive proof, having given warning, promises, and threats (6:149).
ZAJJAJ:v3p378/r5.anchor: ما للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل، ولله الحجة البالغة وقد بشر وأنذر، ووعد وأوعد.

ASAD-NOTES:20:122/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:122/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:122/r3.claim: Turning away from remembrance brings a narrow life and blindness on Resurrection Day.
ASAD-NOTES:20:122/r3.anchor: his shall be a life of narrow scope; [109] and on the Day of Resurrection

ASAD-NOTES:20:122#n109/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:122#n109/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:122#n109/r1.claim: The narrow life is sterile and spiritually constricted, lacking real meaning or purpose, and it becomes a source of hereafter suffering.
ASAD-NOTES:20:122#n109/r1.anchor: sterile and spiritually narrow, without any real meaning or purpose: and this, as is indicated in the subsequent clause

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p497/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p497/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p497/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ḍank as severe and cites a poet describing a tight, difficult pass.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p497/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: الضنك الشديد. واستشهد بقول الشاعر: والخيل قد لحقتْ بها في مأزقٍ. . . ضَنْكٍ نواحيه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p497/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p497/r5.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p497/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says ḍank means severe narrowness; it behaves as a verbal-noun adjective unchanged for singular, dual, plural, masculine, and feminine.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p497/r5.anchor: معناها عند الفراء، الضيقة الشديدة، بالتأنيث

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r1.speaker: الطبري والقرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r1.claim: Exegetes differ over what the constricted life consists of: grave punishment, unlawful earnings, or the fruit of zaqqūm.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r1.anchor: قيل عذاب القبر، وقيل الكسب الحرام، وقيل الزقوم (الطبري، القرطبي.)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.claim: The Qur’an uses ḍank only here as a warning to those who turn from God’s reminder, who will be raised blind.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.anchor: والقرآن لم يستعمل ضنكاً إلا في هذا الموضع، نذيراً لمن أعرض عن ذكره تعالى، يحشره سبحانه يوم القيامة أعمى.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r3.claim: Ḍīq describes the distress of the three who stayed behind at Tabūk without hypocrisy, the Prophet’s constricted chest, and Lot’s distress over his guests.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r3.anchor: وأما الضيق، فجاء في ضيق النفس والأرض على الثلاثة الذين خلفوا عن الخروج مع الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في غزوة تبوك، لغير نفاق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r4.claim: The Qur’an also uses ḍīq for the cramped place of punishment in Hell, as in the description in Sūrat al-Furqān.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r4.anchor: وجاء الضيق في سياق عذاب الآخرة، في آية الفرقان 13

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r5.claim: She judges ḍank to be a more intense constriction, evoking a bottleneck and choking cough, while ḍīq is broader in use.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r5.anchor: يبدو أن الضنك، في البيان القرآني، أشد الضيق وهو في الشاهد للمأزق وضنك السعال يأخذ بالخناق.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r6.claim: Ḍīq is the opposite of spaciousness, literally or figuratively, and can describe physical confinement, emotional distress, or punishment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r6.anchor: وأما الضيق، فأعمُّ في الدلالة من الضنك، يكون من عذابٍ كآية الفرقان، ويكون من ضيق الصدر هماً وكربا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r1.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisai use imāla in both occurrences of aʿmā, in 20:124 and 20:125.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r1.anchor: أبو بكر عن عاصم (أعمى) و (أعمى) [طه/ 124، 125] مكسورتان

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r2.claim: Hafs from Asim reads both occurrences with fatḥa; Nafi is between imāla and fatḥa, while Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Amir use fatḥa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r2.anchor: حفص عن عاصم بفتحهما. نافع بين الكسر والفتح. أبو عمرو بفتحهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r3.claim: Both imāla and its absence are acceptable here; the author says the matter was discussed earlier.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p249#2/r3.anchor: الإمالة وتركها جميعا حسنان في هذا، وقد ذكر فيما مر قبل

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r6.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r6.claim: Abān ibn Taghlib reads ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى in the jussive, coordinated with the conditional جواب phrase فإن له معيشة ضنكا.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك ما يروى عن أبان بن تغلب: "ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى"2، بالجزم.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r7.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r7.claim: The jussive is licensed by coordination with the conditional answer; similarly, Abū ʿAmr reads فأصدق وأكون in the jussive.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p59/r7.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: هو معطوف على موضع قوله عز وجل: "فإن له معيشة ضنكا"، وموضع ذلك جزم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#4/r1.claim: Qatada glosses constricted living as narrowness, saying it is described as constricted in the Fire.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ معيشة ضنكا ﴾ قال الضنك الضيق يقال ضنكا في النار

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri says the constricted life is the grave, which tightens around a person until his ribs cross one another.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال ﴿ فإن له معيشة ضنكا ﴾ قال يضيق عليه قبره حتى تختلف أضلاعه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the person is blind on Judgment Day in the sense that he has no argument to offer.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى ﴾ قال أعمى عن حجته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r2.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the general meaning: dhikr can mean the Qur’an or any divine scripture, and signs can mean proofs generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r2.anchor: والمختار العموم أن يقول : الذكر يقع على القرآن وعلى سائر الكتب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r3.claim: Dhikr is also explained as guidance, since it causes remembrance of God and worship; the effect is named while the cause is intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276/r3.anchor: وقد فسر الذكر أيضا هنا بالهدى لأنه سبب ذكره تعالى وعبادته سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r7.claim: Turning away from remembrance means failing to follow it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r7.anchor: والمراد من الاعراض عن الذكر عدم الاتباع فكانه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r8.claim: Ḍank means constricted and severe; as a verbal noun/adjective it describes masculine or feminine and any number, with feminine here following the noun’s original gender.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r8.anchor: أي ضيقة شديدة وهو مصدر ضنك وكذا ضناكة ولذا يوصف به المذكر والمؤنث

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan reads ḍankā with feminine alif and imāla, construing it as an adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( ضنكى ) بألف التأنيث ككرى وبالامالة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as severe in every respect and cites a line describing a narrow, intensely confined pass.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس تفسيره بالشديد من كل وجه وأنشد قول الشاعر : والخيل قد لحقت بنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r11.speaker: عطاء وابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r11.claim: The apparent meaning is a constricted life in this world; this interpretation is transmitted from ʿAta and Ibn Jubayr.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r11.anchor: والمتبادر أن تلك المعيشة له في الدنيا وروي ذلك عن عطاء وابن جبير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r12.claim: Worldly life is constricted for the disbeliever because he is consumed by greed, acquisition, fear of loss, and miserliness, unlike the believer who seeks the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r12.anchor: ووجه ضيق معيشة الكافر المعرض في الدنيا أنه شديد الحرص على الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r13.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r13.claim: Another explanation takes ḍank as a life without good, a burden for the disbeliever and added punishment on Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : الضنك حجاز عما لا خير فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says wealth given to a servant who does not fear God in its use has no good and is constricted livelihood; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits this gloss.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r14.anchor: مما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس أنه قال في الآية : يقول كل مال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r15.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r15.claim: Some say this life is called constricted because it causes constriction on Judgment Day, naming the cause by its effect; reports from ʿIkrima and Malik ibn Dinar point this way.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r15.anchor: وقيل : المراد من كونها ضنكا إنها سبب للضنك يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r16.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري وأبو صالح والربيع والسدي ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r16.claim: These early authorities interpret the constricted life as punishment in the grave.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r16.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وأبي سعيد الخدري وأبي صالح والربيع والسدي ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r17.claim: Al-Bahr transmits from Ibn Abbas that the verse concerned al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad al-Makhzumi and means the grave’s crushing pressure until his ribs diverge; it is also reported as Prophetic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r17.anchor: وفي البحر عن ابن عباس أن الآية نزلت في الأسود بن عبد الأسد المخزومي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r18.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r18.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying the believer’s grave is spacious and luminous, while the verse refers to the unbeliever’s grave punishment by ninety-nine multiheaded serpents until resurrection; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p276#2/r18.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) المؤمن في قبره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet interpreting the constricted life as grave punishment; one wording says the grave narrows until the ribs diverge, another calls it the grave’s squeeze. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال : قال رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r2.claim: Those who place the constricted life before the great Resurrection count what happens after death as part of worldly life.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r2.anchor: ومن قال : الدنيا ماقبل القيامة الكبرى قال : مايكون بعد الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r3.claim: Another view places the constricted life in Hell on Judgment Day; al-Hasan’s view is transmitted by Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنها تكون يوم القيامة في جهنم وأخرج ذلك ابن أبي شيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Hellish livelihood consists of thorns, zaqqum, ghislin, and darīʿ, and that livelihood exists only in the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن زيد قال : المعيشة الضنك في النار شوك وزقوم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r5.claim: If grave reports are sound, al-Alusi says their meaning must be followed; if not, the worldly-life reading is preferable because the resurrection clause follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r5.anchor: وإن لم تصح كان الأولى القول بأنها في الدنيا لا في الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r6.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r6.claim: A group including Aban ibn Taghlib reads the r of wa-naḥshuruhu as quiescent, as lightening or as a jussive coordinated with the conditional answer fa-inna lahu.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r6.anchor: وقرأت فرقة منهم أبان بن تغلب ( ونحشره ) بإسكان الراء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r7.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r7.claim: Ibn Khalawayh attributes to Aban a reading with quiescent hā, treating connected speech like a pause; al-Bahr prefers the dialect of Banu Kilab and ʿUqayl, who quiesce such pronouns.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r7.anchor: ونقل ابن خالويه عن أبان أنه قرأ ( ونحشره ) بسكون الهاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r8.speaker: فرقة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r8.claim: Another group reads yaḥshuruhu with yāʾ rather than naḥshuruhu with nūn.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r9.claim: The apparent meaning of blind is lacking physical sight, as in the passage describing people gathered blind, mute, and deaf.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p277/r9.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد فاقد البصر كما في قوله تعالى ( ونحشره يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r4.claim: The blindness and deafness are later removed, as indicated by the verse “How clearly they will hear and see on the day they come to Us.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r4.anchor: وكذا اليكم والصمم يزيلهما الله تعالى عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the unbeliever is first resurrected seeing and then blinded; thus “I had been seeing” describes the beginning of resurrection. Al-Alusi says blindness apparently is later removed too.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r5.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه أن الكافر يحشر أولا بصيرا ثم يعمى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r6.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r6.claim: ʿIkrima says the person sees nothing except the Fire; al-Alusi suggests this may apply only at some point that Day, since otherwise the person could not read his record.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r6.anchor: وعن عكرمة أنه لايى شئ إلا النار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r7.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل والضحاك وأبو صالح وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r7.claim: These authorities, in one report from Ibn Abbas, take blindness as lack of proof or insight, and “I had been seeing” as knowing God’s proof and being able to argue in worldly life; Ibrahim ibn ʿUrfa chose this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r7.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد ومقاتل والضحاك وأبي صالح هي رواية عن ابن عباس أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r8.speaker: إبراهيم ابن عرفة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r8.claim: Ibrahim ibn ʿUrfa supports the insight reading with 22:46: the eyes are not blind, but the hearts within the chests are blind.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r8.anchor: واختار ذلك إبراهيم ابن عرفة وقال كلما ذكر الله سبحانه في كتابه العمى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r9.claim: On the insight reading, God says the person was made blind to the argument that could aid him because he abandoned the proofs; as he left them in life, he is left blind forever.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r9.anchor: وحاصل الجواب علية إني حشرتك أعمى القلب لاتهتدي إلى ما يناجيك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r10.claim: Another explanation is that the person is bewildered, unable to devise ways to ward off punishment, like a blind person confused by what he cannot see.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r10.anchor: وقيل : المراد بأعمى متحيرا لايدري مايصنع من الحيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r1.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf use imala on both occurrences of aʿmā because it is a defective-yāʾ form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف ( أعمى ) بالإمالة في الموضعين لأنه من ذوات الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r2.claim: Abu ʿAmr uses imala at the first occurrence only, because it is an especially changeable verse ending and stopping point.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279/r2.anchor: وأمال أبو عمرو في الأول فقط لكونه جديرا بالتغيير لكونه رأس الآية ومحل الوقف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p289/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289/r7.claim: Turning away from remembrance means turning toward the lower world; material attraction and greed produce a constricted life through obsessive attachment to possessions and miserliness.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r1.speaker: some interpreters
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r1.claim: Some say that turning from remembrance darkens one’s time and disrupts one’s livelihood, while remembrance brings certainty and trust, ease, generosity with what one has, and contentment with what one lacks.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p289#2/r1.anchor: لا يعرض أحد عن ذكر ربه سبحانه إلا اظلم عليه وقته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r5.claim: Turning away from God’s reminder means not believing in the Qur’an and not following it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r5.anchor: ومن أعرض عن ذكري} يعني: القرآن، فلم يؤمن به ولم يتبعه، {فإن له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r6.claim: A straitened life means a narrow or constricted life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r6.anchor: فإن له معيشة ضنكا} ضيقا، روي عن ابن مسعود

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة وأبو سعيد الخدري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Hurayra, and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī identify the straitened life as the punishment of the grave.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r7.anchor: روي عن ابن مسعود، وأبي هريرة، وأبي سعيد الخدري أنهم قالوا: هو عذاب القبر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r8.claim: Abū Saʿīd says the grave presses the person until his ribs shift out of place.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو سعيد: يضغط حتى تختلف أضلاعه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r9.claim: A report in some musnads, attributed to the Prophet, says the grave closes until the ribs shift and torment continues until resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r9.anchor: وفي بعض المسانيد مرفوعا. "يلتئم عليه القبر حتى تختلف أضلاعه فلا يزال يعذب حتى يبعث"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the constricted life is the food of Hell: zaqqūm, ḍarīʿ, and ghislin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو الزقوم والضريع والغسلين في النار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r11.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r11.claim: ʿIkrima explains the phrase as unlawful gain or conduct.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r11.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هو الحرام. وقال الضحاك: هو الكسب الخبيث.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r12.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r12.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains it as ill-gotten earnings.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses the straitened life as misery.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r13.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال: الشقاء. وروي عنه أنه قال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r14.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās says wealth, little or much, brings no good if a person is not pious; even the wealthy who reject truth can feel constricted because they distrust God’s provision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r14.anchor: وروي عنه أنه قال: كل مال أعطي العبد قل أم كثر فلم يتق فيه فلا خير فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r15.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r15.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says God removes contentment, leaving the person unable to feel full.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p300#2/r15.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: يسلبه القناعة حتى لا يشبع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the resurrected person’s blindness as blindness of sight.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أعمى البصر. وقال مجاهد أعمى عن الحجة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301/r2.claim: Mujāhid interprets the blindness as being blind to the proof.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r1.claim: God's remembrance here is the guidance that remembers Him and calls people to worship Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r1.anchor: عن الهدى الذاكر لي والداعي إلى عبادتي.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r2.claim: Ḍankan means narrow; as a verbal noun used adjectivally, it has the same form for masculine and feminine.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r2.anchor: ضيقا مصدر وصف به ولذلك يستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r3.claim: Another reading is ḍankā, on the pattern sukrā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r3.anchor: وقرىء { ضنكى } كسكرى، وذلك لأن مجامع همته

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r4.claim: The denier fixates on worldly goods, struggles to increase them, and fears their loss, unlike the believer who seeks the hereafter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r4.anchor: مجامع همته ومطامح نظره تكون إلى أعراض الدنيا متهالكا على ازديادها خائفا على انتقاصها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r5.claim: God may narrow life through unbelief and expand it through faith's blessing, as the cited verses show.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r5.anchor: كما قال وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة [البقرة: 61]

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r6.claim: Other explanations identify the constrained life with the thorny plant and zaqqūm in Hell, or with punishment in the grave.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r6.anchor: وقيل هو الضريع والزقوم في النار، وقيل عذاب القبر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r7.claim: The hāʾ may be vowelless like a pause form, or the verb jussive, coordinated with the conditional response's syntactic position.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r7.anchor: قرىء بسكون الهاء على لفظ الوقف وبالجزم عطفا على محل

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r8.claim: The person is gathered blind in physical sight or in the heart; Bayḍāwī indicates the first is supported.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:124/r8.anchor: أعمى البصر أو القلب ويؤيد الأول

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r10.claim: Turning away from remembrance is deliberate abandonment of what benefits a person; remembrance here means God's guidance.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r11.claim: The feminine form of maʿisha diminishes it, while ḍankan is an especially harsh verbal noun whose form is unchanged across gender and number.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r11.anchor: حقرها سبحانه بالتأنيث ثم وصفها بأفظع وصف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r12.claim: The life is constricted because misguidance inevitably ends in distress, even when outwardly spacious; the cause is named for its eventual effect, as greed, miserliness, rivalries, and worry leave no contentment or security.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r13.speaker: أنس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r13.claim: A report agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim says that if Adam's son had a valley of gold he would seek another, then a third, and only dust fills his belly; God accepts the repentance of the repentant.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r13.anchor: متفق عليه عن أنس رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r14.claim: By contrast, one wholly devoted to remembrance is content and satisfied; remembrance expands the breast and illuminates the heart, so inward meaning matters more than outward appearances.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r14.anchor: مستكثر ن ذكر الله الشارح للصدور

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person rises from the grave seeing but becomes blind when driven to the gathering place.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r15.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إذا خرج من القبر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r16.claim: The author favors the nearer literal reading that blindness applies to some misguided people, which fits the statement that they will see clearly when they come to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p53/r16.anchor: بعض أهل الضلال ليجتمع مع قوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r1.claim: A sound report from Ibn Umar quotes the Prophet saying that wrongdoing is layers of darkness on the Day of Resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r1.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r1.claim: Ibn Majah reports from Ibn Masud that the person who makes the Hereafter the sole concern is spared worldly worry, whereas one whose concerns fragment across worldly affairs may perish in any valley without God's care.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r1.anchor: سمعت نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r2.claim: Ibn Majah reports from Zayd ibn Thabit that a worldly aim scatters one's affairs and leaves poverty before one's eyes, while an intention for the Hereafter gathers affairs and puts richness in the heart.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت رضي اله عنه : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v5p607/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet interprets the constricted life as punishment in the grave; one version says the grave presses until the ribs overlap, another calls it the grave's squeeze.
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري مرفوعا في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: عذاب القبر وفي لفظ عبد الرزاق قال: يضيق عليه قبره حتى تختلف أضلاعه

DURR-FULL:v5p607/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r3.claim: Abu Said says the constricted life means that ninety-nine dragons torment the person in the grave.
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: إن المعيشة الضنك: أن يسلط عليه تسعة وتسعون تنينا تنهشه في القبر

DURR-FULL:v5p607/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r4.claim: The Prophet says the constricted life is a grave punishment in which ninety-nine snakes bite the person's flesh until resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} قال: المعيشة الضنك التي قال الله: إنه يسلط عليه تسعة وتسعون حية تنهش لحمه حتى تقوم الساعة

DURR-FULL:v5p607/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r5.claim: Another report from the Prophet identifies the constricted life simply as punishment in the grave.
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} قال: عذاب القبر

DURR-FULL:v5p607/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r6.claim: A report from the Prophet contrasts the believer's spacious, illuminated grave with the unbeliever's grave punishment by ninety-nine dragons or snakes, each with seven heads, tormenting him until resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: المؤمن في قبره في روضة خضراءويرحب

DURR-FULL:v5p607/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r7.claim: Ibn Masud reports that a believer answers the grave's questions about Lord, religion, and Prophet correctly and is confirmed by God; his account continues in the next segment.
DURR-FULL:v5p607/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إذا حدثتكم بحديث أنبأتكم بتصديق ذلك من كتاب الله إن المؤمن إذا وضع في قبره أجلس فيه فيقال له: من ربك وما دينك ومن نبيك

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r1.claim: Ibn Masud continues: the believer's grave expands and gives comfort, while the unbeliever cannot answer its questions and is constricted and punished; he cites God's promise to make believers firm in 14:27 and the warning of this verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r1.anchor: فيوسع له في قبره ويروح له فيه ثم قرأ عبد الله

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the constricted life as misery.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: الشقاء

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r3.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas locates the hardship in the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: شدة عليه في النار

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r4.claim: In a question from Nafi ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas defines ضنك as severe hardship in every respect and cites an Arabic poem using ضنك for a constricted, severe place.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله: {معيشة ضنكا}

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r5.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the constricted life as punishment in the grave.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} قال: عذاب القبر

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r6.speaker: أبو صالح والربيع
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r6.claim: Abu Salih and al-Rabiʿ give the same interpretation: punishment in the grave.

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r7.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r7.claim: Al-Hasan glosses constricted livelihood as an adversary or disputant.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r7.anchor: عن الحسن قال: المعيشة الضنك خصم

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says wealth, whether little or much, has no good when its recipient does not obey God with it; that is constricted livelihood.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: يقول: كل مال أعطيته عبدا من عبادي قل أو كثر لا يطيعني فيه فلا خير فيه وهو الضنك في المعيشة

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses ضنك as narrow or constricted.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: ضيقة

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r10.claim: Ikrima says a person may be given wealth yet made to earn it unlawfully, so it becomes constricted for him in Hell.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r10.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: الضنك من المعيشة إذا وسع الله على عبده أن يجعل معيشته من الحرام

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r11.speaker: مالك بن دينار
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r11.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says God turns a person's livelihood into unlawful provision, which he consumes tainted until he dies and is punished for it.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r11.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: يحول الله رزقه في الحرام فلا يطعمه إلا رانا حتى يموت فيعذبه عليه

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r12.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak also interprets constricted life as evil deeds and impure provision.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r12.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: العمل السيء والرزق الخبيث

DURR-FULL:v5p608/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd says the phrase means life in Hell, among thorns, Zaqqum, ghislin, and dariʿ; he rejects the grave and worldly life here, since true life is only in the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v5p608/r13.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: في النار شوك وزقوم وغسلين والضريع وليس في القبر ولا في الدنيا معيشة ما المعيشة والحياة إلا في الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r1.claim: Mujahid defines it as constricted life, with the grave made tight for the person.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد {معيشة ضنكا} ضيقة يضيق عليه قبره

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r2.claim: Mujahid also glosses the constricted life as provision.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} قال: رزقا

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r3.claim: Mujahid says the unbeliever is raised blind to the proof.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} قال: رزقا {ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى} قال: عن الحجة

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r6.claim: Abu Salih interprets being raised blind as having no proof.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r6.anchor: عن أبي صالح في قوله: {ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى} قال: ليس له حجة

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r7.claim: Ikrima says everything is obscured from the person except Hell; he sees only the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى} قال: عمي عليه كل شيء إلا جهنم وفي لفظ قال: لا يبصر إلا النار

BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r1.claim: God’s reminder means the scripture that reminds people of Him and the messenger who calls them to Him; dhikr may mean the Quran or other divine books.
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r1.anchor: أي : الكتاب الذاكر لي والرسول الداعي إلي والذكر يقع على القرآن وغيره من كتب الله

BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r2.claim: Ḍank is a verbal noun used adjectivally for a constricted life, with the same form for masculine and feminine.
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r2.anchor: {معيشة ضنكا} ضيقا مصدر وصف به مبالغة ولذلك يستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث

BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r3.claim: The heedless person’s life is constricted because attention is fixed on worldly aims, endless accumulation, and fear of loss; God may also constrict an unbeliever for disbelief and expand a believer through faith.
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r3.anchor: والمعنى معيشة ذات ضنك وذلك لأن نظره مقصور على أغراض الدنيا وهو يتهالك على ازديادها وخائف من انتقاصها

BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r4.claim: A punishment for sin is cramped living, including being returned to the lower self, species, and material forms.
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r4.anchor: واعلم أن من عقوبة المعصية ضيق المعيشة والرد إلى النفس والأجناس والأكوان من ضيق المعيشة

BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r7.claim: The inward commentary reads turning away as failing to keep remembrance while following guidance; the result is a heart tormented by the veil and a closed door, since remembrance unlocks hearts.
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r7.anchor: {ومن أعرض عن ذكرى} أي : عن ملازمة ذكري في اتباع هداي أي : إذا جاءه {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} أي : يعذب قلبه بذل الحجاب وسد الباب

BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r8.claim: The Persian couplet calls remembrance of God the key that opens the soul’s door and the food of the king; it is the saints’ continual sustenance.
BURSEVI:v5p338#3/r8.anchor: ذكر حق مفتاح باشد أى سعيد تا تبكشايى در جان بى كليد ون ملك ذكر خدارا كن غذا اين بود دائم معاش اوليا

BURSEVI:v5p339/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r1.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p339/r1.claim: Al-Hashr can mean resurrection or gathering; the first sense is intended here.
BURSEVI:v5p339/r1.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : الحشر يجيىء بمعنى البعث والجمع والأول هو المراد هنا

BURSEVI:v5p339/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339/r2.claim: The person is literally deprived of sight at the Resurrection, as in the verse about being gathered blind, mute, and deaf.
BURSEVI:v5p339/r2.anchor: فاقد البصر كما في قوله تعالى :

BURSEVI:v5p339/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r3.speaker: عرائس البقلى
BURSEVI:v5p339/r3.claim: The inward blindness is ignorance of the Real's existence in this life, continuing into the next.
BURSEVI:v5p339/r3.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلى" : يعني جاهلا بوجود الحق كما كان جاهلا في الدنيا

BURSEVI:v5p339/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r4.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v5p339/r4.claim: Ali says that whoever does not know God in this world will not know Him in the next.
BURSEVI:v5p339/r4.anchor: كما قال علي رضي الله عنه : من لم يعرف الله في الدنيا لا يعرفه في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r1.claim: Ḍank is a verbal noun from ḍanuka and retains one form regardless of the gender of its described noun, hence its use with feminine maʿīsha.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r1.anchor: والضنك : مصدر ضنك ، من باب كرم ضناكة وضنكا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r2.speaker: عنترة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r2.claim: Ḍank means narrow and can figuratively describe hardship; ʿAntara's verse uses it of a difficult place to stay.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r2.anchor:
قال عنترة :
إن يلحقوا أكرر وإن يستلحموا
أشدد وإن نزلوا بضنك أنزل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r3.claim: The narrow life is inner distress: a person anxiously accumulates possessions and neglects virtue, even when outward comfort makes life look good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r3.anchor: وهو هنا بمعنى عسر الحال من اضطراب البال وتبلبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r8.claim: Ḍank means harsh, difficult life or dwelling, including places of war; Antara's line is cited for the word.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r8.anchor: والضنك النكد الشاق من العيش أو المنازل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r9.claim: The passage describes another afterlife state: the rejecter is gathered blind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r9.anchor: ثم أخبر عن حالة أخرى هي أيضا في يوم القيامة وهي حشرهم عميا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r10.claim: The next verse says afterlife punishment is more severe and lasting; the narrow life and blindness described are types of that punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r10.anchor: فكأنه ذكر نوعا من عذاب الآخرة ثم أخبر أن عذاب الآخرة أشد وأبقى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r11.claim: Some read ونحشره with nūn, others ويحشره with yāʾ, including a variant with rāʾ quiescent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r11.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «ونحشره» بالنون، وقرأت فرقة «ويحشره» بالياء وقرأت فرقة «ويحشره» بسكون الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r12.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r12.claim: A group reads أعمى with imāla.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r13.claim: One group says blindness means blindness of insight; Ibn Atiyya objects that unbelievers already have this blindness and would not fear being raised that way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r13.anchor: العمى هنا هو عمى البصيرة عن الحجة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r14.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers physical blindness, though blindness of insight exists under either interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r14.anchor: وهذا هو الأوجه مع أن عمى البصيرة حاصل في الوجهين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r15.claim: If the blindness is physical, the description of criminals as blue-eyed in 20:102 must refer to two groups or two scenes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r15.anchor: فلا بد أن يتأول فيها مع هذه إما أنها في طائفتين أو في موطنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r1.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r1.claim: ʿAta interprets “My remembrance” as God's admonition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ومن أعرض عن ذكري قال عطاء عن موعظتي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r2.claim: Ibn al-Saib takes “My remembrance” to mean the Qur'an, which the person neither believes nor follows.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r2.anchor: وقال ابن السائب عن القرآن ولم يؤمن به ولم يتبعه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r3.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses the phrase as a constricted life; ḍank can describe masculine or feminine nouns without a feminine ending and applies to any narrow life, place, or dwelling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة معناه معيشة ضيقة والضنك يوصف به الأنثى والذكر بغير هاء وكل عيش أو مكان أو منزل ضيق فهو ضنك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r4.claim: An anonymous verse uses ḍank to describe a constricted situation, illustrating the word's usage.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the word's root meaning is narrowness and hardship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج الضنك أصله في اللغة الضيق والشدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r6.speaker: رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet identified the constricted life as the unbeliever's grave punishment: ninety-nine serpents blow on, sting, and scratch him until the Resurrection; no grading is stated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r6.anchor: أحدها أنها عذاب القبر روى أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أتدرون ما المعيشة الضنك قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال عذاب الكافر في قبره والذي نفسي بيده إنه ليسلط عليه تسعة وتسعون تنينا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, and al-Suddi also identify the constricted life as punishment in the grave.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r7.anchor: وممن ذهب إلى أنه عذاب القبر ابن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r8.claim: ʿAta transmits from Ibn Abbas that the phrase means the grave's crushing pressure, which makes the ribs shift.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r8.anchor: والثاني أنه ضغطة القبر حتى تختلف أضلاعه فيه رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r9.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r9.claim: The view that constricted life is hardship in Hell is transmitted from Ibn Abbas by al-Dahhak and also held by al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd; Ibn al-Saib says its food is darīʿ and zaqqum.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r9.anchor: قال ابن السائب وتلك المعيشة من الضريع والزقوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that it means unlawful earnings: good avenues are closed to the person, leaving only forbidden livelihood; al-Dahhak and ʿIkrima call it ill-gotten income.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r10.anchor: والرابع أن المعيشة الضنك كسب الحرام روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال المعيشة الضنك أن تضيق عليه أبواب الخير فلا يهتدى لشيء منها وله معيشة حرام يركض فيها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r11.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r11.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits from Ibn Abbas that the constricted life is wealth whose owner does not fear God in using it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r11.anchor: والخامس أن المعيشة الضنك المال الذي لا يتقي الله صاحبه فيه رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r12.claim: The five explanations locate the constricted life in three settings: the grave, worldly life, or Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r12.anchor: فخرج في مكان المعيشة ثلاثة أقوال أحدها القبر والثاني الدنيا والثالث جهنم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r13.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r13.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and Hafs from ʿAsim read both occurrences with fatḥa on the two mīms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r13.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابو عمرو وابن عامر وحفص عن عاصم أعمى حشترتني أعمى بفتح الميمين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r14.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r14.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read both occurrences with kasra on the two mīms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r14.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بكسرهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r15.speaker: نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r15.claim: Nafiʿ reads the two occurrences between kasra and fatḥa.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r16.claim: Abu Salih reports from Ibn Abbas that the person emerges from the grave seeing, then becomes blind while being driven to the assembly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p330#3/r16.anchor: أحدهما أعمى البصر روى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال إذا أخرج من القبر خرج بصيرا فاذا سيق إلى المحشر عمي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332/r1.speaker: مجاهد وأبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332/r1.claim: Mujahid and Abu Salih say the person is blind to the proof; al-Zajjaj explains that no guidance argument remains against God after the messengers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332/r1.anchor: والثاني أعمى عن الحجة قاله مجاهد وأبو صالح قال الزجاج معناه فلا حجة له يهتدي بها لأنه ليس للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r5.claim: Turning away from God's reminder means opposing His command and revelation to His messenger, neglecting it, and taking guidance from elsewhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r5.anchor: أي: خالف أمري، وما أنزلته على رسولي، أعرض عنه وتناساه وأخذ من غيره هداه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r6.claim: The constricted life is worldly inward distress: no tranquility or open heart, but anxiety, doubt, and uncertainty, even amid outward luxury.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r6.anchor: أي: في الدنيا، فلا طمأنينة له، ولا انشراح لصدره، بل صدره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report transmitted by Ali ibn Abi Talha, glosses the constricted life as misery.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r7.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r8.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas as saying that wealth, little or much, brings no good if its recipient does not fear God; this is constricted living.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r9.claim: Some deniers had worldly abundance yet a constricted life: they distrusted God to sustain them, and their disbelief and poor expectation made life difficult.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r9.anchor: ويقال: إن قوما ضلالا أعرضوا عن الحق، وكانوا في سعة من الدنيا متكبرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r10.speaker: الضحاك، عكرمة، مالك بن دينار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak, Ikrima, and Malik ibn Dinar each explain the constricted living as evil deeds and corrupt provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r10.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو العمل السيئ، والرزق الخبيث، وكذا قال عكرمة، ومالك بن دينار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r11.speaker: أبو سعيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r11.claim: Abu Sa'id says the constricted life is the grave squeezing its occupant until his ribs press against each other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي سعيد في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: يضيق عليه قبره، حتى تختلف أضلاعه فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r12.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r12.claim: Abu Hatim al-Razi identifies al-Nu'man ibn Abi Ayyash as kunya Abu Salama, the transmitter named in the preceding report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r12.anchor: قال أبو حاتم الرازي: النعمان بن أبي عياش (3) يكنى أبا سلمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Abu Sa'id a Prophetic gloss, grave squeeze; Ibn Kathir says the stopped version is more authentic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p322#2/r13.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet describing the believer's spacious, lit grave and the unbeliever's grave torment by ninety-nine many-headed dragons; Ibn Kathir calls this raised version very munkar.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: المؤمن في قبره في روضة خضراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r2.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits Abu Hurayra's Prophetic explanation that constricted living is punishment by ninety-nine snakes biting the sinner until resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الله عز وجل: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r3.claim: A second report from Abu Hurayra identifies the constricted living as grave punishment; Ibn Kathir grades its chain good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p323/r3.anchor: عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r1.speaker: مجاهد، أبو صالح، السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r1.claim: Mujahid, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi say the person will have no proof or argument.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد، وأبو صالح، والسدي: لا حجة له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r2.claim: Ikrima says everything will be obscured from him except Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة: عمي عليه كل شيء إلا جهنم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir considers that the denier is raised or brought to the Fire blind in sight and insight, as in 17:97.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد: أنه يحشر أو يبعث (3) إلى النار أعمى البصر والبصيرة أيضا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.claim: Some commentators include neglecting Quran recitation, allowing it to be forgotten, and failing to care for it within turning away from God’s remembrance; Ibn Kathir says this is part, though not the whole, of the verse’s intent and is grave negligence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.anchor: وقد أدخل بعض المفسرين هذا المعنى في قوله تعالى: {ومن أعرض عن ذكري

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r4.claim: Ḍank means narrow and difficult; it is indeclinable because it originated as a verbal noun.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r4.anchor: والضنك: الضيق والصعب، منزل ضنك أي: ضيق، وعيش ضنك لا يثنى ولا يجمع ولا يؤنث؛ لأن أصله المصدر

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r20.claim: Turning away from God’s remembrance means turning away from the Quran and acting on it.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r20.anchor: ومن أعرض عن ذكري عن القرآن والعمل بما فيه

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r21.speaker: مجاهد، وقتادة، وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r21.claim: They interpret the constricted life as a narrow, difficult life.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r21.anchor: قيل: عيشا ضيقا، عن مجاهد، وقتادة، وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v7p4758/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r22.speaker: الحسن، وقتادة، وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r22.claim: They interpret the constricted life as the thorny plant and zaqqum in Hell.
JISHUMI:v7p4758/r22.anchor: وقيل: هو الضريع والزقوم في النار، عن الحسن، وقتادة، وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v7p4761/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r8.claim: These verses show that human acts originate from human agents, contradicting the compulsion doctrine.
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r8.anchor: ويدل قوله: (فمن اتبع هداي) و(ومن أعرض عن ذكري) على أن فعل العبد حادث من جهته

JISHUMI:v7p4761/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4761/r10.claim: The passage teaches that the deniers will be resurrected blind.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r1.claim: Ḍank is a verbal noun that describes either masculine or feminine nouns.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r1.anchor: مصدر يستوي في الوصف به المذكر والمؤنث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r2.claim: A variant reads ḍankā on the faʿlā pattern.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r3.claim: Surrender, contentment, and trust in God’s allotment produce easy spending and a comfortable life; greed and miserliness constrict the life of one who turns from religion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r3.anchor: مع الدين التسليم والقناعة والتوكل على الله وعلى قسمته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r4.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r4.claim: An unnamed Sufi says turning from God darkens one’s time and unsettles one’s provision.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r4.anchor: قال بعض المتصوفة : لا يعرض أحد عن ذكر ربه إلا أظلم عليه وقته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r5.claim: Some unbelievers face humiliation for disbelief; other verses promise blessings for faith, obeying scripture, seeking forgiveness, and steadfastness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r5.anchor: قال الله تعالى : { وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة وباءوا بغضب من الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r6.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the constricted life is al-Ḍarīʿ and al-Zaqqūm in Hell.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r6.anchor: وعن الحسن : هو الضريع والزقوم في النار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r7.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī identifies it with punishment in the grave.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r7.anchor: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري : ( 687 ) ( عذاب القبر )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r8.claim: The jussive ‘We gather him’ coordinates with the syntactic position of the conditional apodosis ‘he will have a constricted life.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r8.anchor: وقرىء { ونحشره } بالجزم عطفا على محل { فإن له معيشة ضنكا }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r9.claim: Another reading gives hāʾ sukūn as in pausal pronunciation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r9.anchor: وقرىء : ( ونحشره ) بسكون الهاء على لفظ الوقف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r10.claim: The blindness parallels 17:97; ‘just as’ means God treats the person as he treated the signs, leaving him blind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r10.anchor: وهذا مثل قوله : { ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما }

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r3.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r3.claim: The constricted life means unlawful earnings.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r4.claim: It is a troubled life, because a person without certainty about compensation spends anxiously.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r4.anchor: أن يكون عيشه منغصا بأن ينفق من لا يوقن بالخلف , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r5.claim: Another view identifies the constricted life as the punishment of the grave.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r5.anchor: أنه عذاب القبر , قاله أبو سعيد الخدري وابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra raises the interpretation that the constricted life is punishment of the grave to the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r6.anchor: وقد رفعه أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r7.claim: Another view is that it means the food of ḍarīʿ and zaqqūm in Hell.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r7.anchor: أنه الطعام الضريع والزقوم في جهنم , قاله الحسن , وقتادة , وابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r8.claim: A further possibility is earning less than one's needs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r8.anchor: ويحتمل خامسا : أن يكسب دون كفايته

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r9.claim: In Arabic, ḍank means narrow or constricted; Antarah's verse speaks of a constricted dwelling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r9.anchor: والضنك في كلامهم الضيق قال , عنترة : إن المنية لو تمثل مثلت … مثلي إذا نزلوا بضنك المنزل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r10.claim: The person may be blind at one time and sighted at another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r10.anchor: أعمى في حال , وبصير في حال

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r11.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r11.claim: The person is blind to the argument or proof.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r12.claim: The person is blind to the paths of good and cannot find any of them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p430/r12.anchor: أعمى عن وجهات الخير لا يهتدي لشيء منها

MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r1.claim: The Prophet says the constricted life is the punishment of the grave.
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المعيشة الضنك عذاب القبر

MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r2.claim: Mujahid says it is a narrow life in which the person's grave is constricted.
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ معيشة ضنكا ﴾ قال ضيقة يضيق عليه قبره

MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r3.claim: Being gathered blind means being blind to the proof.
MUJAHID:v1p404#3/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى ﴾ قال أعمى عن الحجة

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r6.claim: Turning away from remembrance means refusing belief in the Qur'an; the warning was revealed about al-Aswad b. Abd al-Aswad al-Makhzumi, whom Hamza killed at Badr by the watering place.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r6.anchor: نزلت فى الأسود بن عبد الأسود المخزومى، قتله حمزة بن عبد المطلب يوم بدر على الحوض

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r7.claim: A constricted life is an evil life, constricted because it is spent disobeying God.
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r7.anchor: { فإن له معيشة ضنكا } يعنى معيشة سوء لأنها فى معاصى الله عز وجل الضنك والضيق

MUQATIL:20:123-125/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:123-125/r8.claim: The person is gathered blind with respect to his argument or proof.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r1.anchor: ﴿ ومن أعرض عن ذكري ﴾ عن القرآن

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r2.claim: “A constricted life” means a narrow life; the verbal noun can describe either masculine or feminine nouns.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r2.anchor: ضيقا وهو مصدر يستوى فى الوصف به المذكر والمونث

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r3.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the person is deprived of contentment and never feels satisfied; submission, contentment, and reliance on God make life good, while turning away brings greed and misery.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r3.anchor: عن ابن جبير يسلبه القناعه حتى لا يشبع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r4.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r4.claim: A Sufi saying holds that turning away from remembrance darkens one’s time and unsettles one’s livelihood.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r4.anchor: كما قال بعض المتصوفة لا يعرض أحدكم عن ذكر ربه إلا أظلم عليه وقته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r5.claim: One explanation is that the person is blind to proof.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the blindness as loss of physical sight.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r7.claim: He prefers physical blindness, comparing it with the statement that people will be gathered on their faces blind.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71/r7.anchor: وهو كقوله ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وهو الوجه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r7.claim: Dhikr may mean God's religion, reciting His Book, and acting by it; it may instead mean the revealed proofs, or the Messenger as the source of the reminder.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r7.anchor: أي ديني، وتلاوة كتابي، والعمل بما فيه. وقيل: عما أنزلت من الدلائل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r8.claim: ضنك describes a constricted dwelling or life and has the same form for singular, dual, masculine, feminine, and plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r8.anchor: أي عيشا ضيقا يقال: منزل ضنك وعيش ضنك يستوي فيه الواحد والاثنان والمذكر والمؤنث

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r9.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r9.claim: Antarah uses بضنك for a constricted or difficult place in two lines, illustrating the word's usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r9.anchor: قال عنترة: إن يلحقوا أكرر وإن يستلحموا أشدد وإن يلفوا بضنك أنزل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r10.claim: A variant reading has ضنكى on the فعلى pattern.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r11.claim: Religion brings submission, contentment, and trust in God and His allotment, so the believer spends easily and lives abundantly; Qurtubi links this to the good life promised in 16:97.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r11.anchor: أن الله عز وجل جعل مع الدين التسليم والقناعة والتوكل عليه وعلى قسمته، فصاحبه ينفق مما رزقه الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r12.claim: Turning from religion lets acquisitive greed and miserliness dominate, making life constricted and dark; one reported saying adds that the person's time darkens and livelihood becomes troubled.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r12.anchor: والمعرض عن الدين مستول عليه الحرص الذي لا يزال يطمح به إلى الازدياد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r13.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r13.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the constricted life as unlawful earnings.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r14.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r14.claim: Al-Hasan interprets it as the food of ḍarīʿ and zaqqum.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r15.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وعبد الله بن مسعود وأبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r15.claim: Qurtubi calls the fourth interpretation correct: punishment in the grave, stated by Abu Saʿid and Ibn Masʿud and reported marfuʿ by Abu Hurayra from the Prophet; the unbeliever's grave tightens until his ribs interlock. No grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r15.anchor: وقول رابع وهو الصحيح أنه عذاب القبر قاله أبو سعيد الخدري وعبد الله بن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r16.claim: The interpretation that a person is blind in one state and sighted in another was discussed at the end of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r16.anchor: قيل: أعمى في حال وبصيرا في حال وقد تقدم في آخر «سبحان».

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r17.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r17.claim: Mujahid says the person is blind to the proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r17.anchor: وقيل: أعمى عن الحجة قاله مجاهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r18.claim: Other explanations say the person is blind to every path of good, or unable to find a way to fend off punishment, like a blind person helpless before what he cannot see.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:123-124/r18.anchor: وقيل: أعمى عن جهات الخير، لا يهتدي لشيء منها. وقيل: عن الحيلة في دفع العذاب عن نفسه

QASHANI:20:124/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:124/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:124/r1.claim: Turning toward the lower world through psychic desire constricts livelihood: a stagnant soul clings to material adornments and possessions, and accumulating them intensifies greed and miserliness.
QASHANI:20:124/r1.anchor: بالتوجه إلى العالم السفلي بالميل النفسي، ضاقت معيشته لغلبة شحه وشدة بخله

QASHANI:20:124/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
