QASHANI:20:124/r2.speaker: بعض الصوفية
QASHANI:20:124/r2.claim: Some Sufis say that whoever turns from remembrance of the Lord finds life darkened and provision troubled.
QASHANI:20:124/r2.anchor: قال بعض الصوفية: لا يعرض أحد عن ذكر ربه إلا أظلم عليه وتشوش عليه رزقه

QASHANI:20:124/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:124/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:124/r3.claim: By contrast, the one who remembers and turns to God lives with certainty and trust, spends what is available, and dispenses with what is absent through reliance on the Lord.
QASHANI:20:124/r3.anchor: بخلاف الذاكر المتوجه إليه فإنه ذو يقين منه وتوكل عليه في سعة من عيشه ورغد

QASHANI:20:124/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:124/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:124/r4.claim: The minor resurrection finds the denier blind to divine light, as in 17:72; innate preparedness and natural light still attest to the blindness caused by entrenched lower-world love, bodily transgression, and forgetting signs.
QASHANI:20:124/r4.anchor: الصغرى على عماه من نور الحق كقوله: ومن كان في هذه أعمى فهو في الآخرة أعمى

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r13.claim: Dhikr may refer to the Qurʾān or to the other scriptures God sent.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r13.anchor: والذكر يقع على القرآن وعلى سائر كتب الله تعالى على ما تقدم بيانه

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r14.claim: A further possible referent for dhikr is the proofs and indications.

RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r15.claim: Ḍank originally means narrowness and hardship; it is a verbal noun that is also used adjectivally.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112/r15.anchor: فالضنك أصله الضيق والشدة وهو مصدر ثم يوصف به

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r1.claim: The phrase means a life characterized by constriction, as though it said a life possessing constriction.

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r2.speaker: جمع من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r2.claim: Some exegetes take the constricted life as worldly: believers who trust God live well, while unbelievers remain greedy, anxious, and sometimes humiliated; revelation links obedience with provision.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r2.anchor: فقال به جمع من المفسرين وذلك لأن المسلم لتوكله على الله يعيش في الدنيا عيشا طيبا

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري وعبد الله بن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r3.claim: They identify the constricted life with punishment in the grave.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r3.anchor: فهذا قول عبد الله بن مسعود وأبي سعيد الخدري وعبد الله بن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra attributes to the Prophet a report that the unbeliever is punished in the grave by ninety-nine dragons.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r4.anchor: ورفعه أبو هريرة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( إن عذاب القبر للكافر قال والذي نفسي بيده

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi and means the grave's pressure that displaces the ribs.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : نزلت الآية في الأسود بن عبد العزى المخزومي والمراد ضغطة القبر تختلف فيها أضلاعه

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r6.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and al-Kalbi understand it as constriction in Hell, where food and drink are agonizing and its inmates neither die nor live.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r6.anchor: فلا يموتون فيها / ولا يحيون وهذا قول الحسن وقتادة والكلبي

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is spiritual constriction: the doors of good close before a person, who cannot find guidance to any good.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r7.anchor: فقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : المعيشة الضنك هي أن تضيق عليه أبواب الخير فلا يهتدي لشيء منها

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r8.speaker: الشبلي
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r8.claim: Al-Shibli explains that the truly afflicted are heedless of God; their punishment is to be left to themselves, an especially constricted condition.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r8.anchor: سئل الشبلي عن قوله عليه السلام : ( إذا رأيتم أهل البلاء فاسألوا الله العافية ) فقال أهل البلاء هم أهل الغفلات عن الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r9.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r9.claim: Ata says the constricted life is that of an unbeliever, who lacks certainty about reward and punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v22p112#2/r9.anchor: وعن عطاء قال : المعيشة الضنك هي معيشة الكافر لأنه غير موقن بالثواب والعقاب

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r1.claim: One reading compares this to 17:97, where people are gathered blind, mute, and deaf; a person may be sighted until being driven to the gathering, then blinded, as discussed at the passage on the blue-eyed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r1.anchor: هذا مثل قوله : { ونحشرهم يوم القيامة على وجوههم عميا وبكما وصما }

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r2.claim: They say the person is blind to the proof; Sa'id ibn Jubayr transmits this interpretation from Ibn Abbas.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد والضحاك ومقاتل : يعني أعمى عن الحجة

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r3.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports Ibn Abbas's interpretation that the blindness is blindness to the proof.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r3.anchor: وهي رواية سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r4.claim: The Qadi calls the proof-blindness interpretation weak: people must recognize the falsity of their former beliefs in the afterlife, so they cannot literally be blind to the distinction between truth and falsehood; it also conflicts with their former sight.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r4.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا القول ضعيف لأن في القيامة لا بد أن يعلمهم الله تعالى بطلان ما كانوا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r5.claim: Razi says the Qadi's objection rests on Mu'tazilite principles and sharply distinguishes his own account from that foundation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r5.anchor: وبين هذه الطريقة وبين طريقة القاضي المبنية على أصول الاعتزال بون شديد

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r6.claim: Razi answers that ignorant souls remain ignorant after leaving their bodies, and this ignorance becomes a source of the greatest spiritual pain in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r6.anchor: واعلم أن تحقيق الجواب عن هذا الاعتراض مأخوذ من أمر آخر وهو أن الأرواح الجاهلة في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r7.speaker: الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r7.claim: Al-Jubba'i takes blindness to mean that the person finds no path to good on Judgment Day and stands bewildered like someone unable to see a way.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r7.anchor: قال الجبائي : المراد من حشره أعمى أنه لا يهتدي يوم القيامة إلى طريق ينال منه خيرا

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r10.claim: Those who interpret constricted life as worldly take the passage to pair worldly hardship for turning from remembrance with blindness in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r10.anchor: ومن فسر المعيشة الضنك بالضيق في الدنيا ، قال إنه تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p57/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p57/r1.claim: Citing Imruʾ al-Qays, Razi says “kafani” takes a little money as its object, while “wa-lam atlub” means he did not seek kingship; assigning both verbs the same object would make the conditional self-contradictory.
RAZI-FULL:v1p57/r1.anchor:
قول امرئ القيس :
فلو أن ما أسعى لأدنى معيشة … كفاني ولم أطلب قليل من المال

QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r11.claim: For a disbeliever who entirely turns from remembrance, the constricted life is in this world, the grave, and the Fire; inwardly it is the loneliness of disbelief and the closing of affairs.
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r11.anchor: الكافر إذا أعرض عن ذكره بالكلية فله المعيشة الضنك في الدنيا ، وفي القبر ، وفي النار ، وبالقلب من حيث وحشة الكفر

QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r12.claim: Turning away from conformity brings repeated abandonment and failure.
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r12.anchor: من أعرض عن الانخراط في قضايا الوفاق انثالت عليه فنون الخذلان

QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r13.claim: Neglecting continual remembrance in the heart scatters it and strips away every source of spiritual life.
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r13.anchor: ومن أعرض عن استدامة ذكره - سبحانه - بالقلب توالت عليه من تفرقة القلب ما يسلب عنه كل روح

QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r14.claim: Abandoning intimacy with remembrance opens the door to satanic and psychic whispers, inner loneliness, and a loss of ease and expansiveness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r14.anchor: ومن أعرض عن الاستئناس بذكره انفتحت عليه وساوس الشيطان وهواجس النفس بما يوجب له وحشة الضمير

QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r15.claim: Neglecting remembrance in solitude brings a harmful companion whose presence grips the heart and fills it with estrangement.
QUSHAYRI:v2p280/r15.anchor: من أعرض عن ذكر الله في الخلوة قيض الله له في الظاهر من القرين السوء ما توجب رؤيته له قبض القلوب

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.claim: Citing a report that a person meets God in the state in which they lived, Qushayri says the worldly blind of heart and the ignorant are resurrected in that condition.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.anchor: في الخبر : ( من كان بحالة لقي الله بها ) فمن كان في الدنيا أعمى القلب يحشر على حالته

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r3.claim: Those who neglect reflection on God's signs in this life are left in punishment without mercy in the next; God's practice repays each person according to their deeds.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r3.anchor: وكما يتركون - اليوم - التدبر في آياته يتركون غدا في العقوبة من غير رحمة على ضعف حالاتهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r4.claim: Qushayri urges people to reflect, take heed, and stop their bad conduct instead of running through heedlessness without turning back.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r4.anchor: أفلا ينظرون فيتفكرون ؟ ثم إذا استبصروا أفلا يعتبرون ؟ وإذا اعتبروا أفلا يزدجرون

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r5.claim: God delayed punishment for this community and did not destroy it because saints remain in the loins of some people; the respite has a set term, but God has not neglected them.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r5.anchor: لولا أن كلمة الله سبقت بتأخير العقوبة عن هذه الأمة ، وأنه لا يستأصلهم لأن جماعة من الأولياء في أصلابهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r6.claim: Although happiness and misery are decreed and God's knowledge encompasses what will occur, striving and effort also belong to the decree.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r6.anchor: فالسعي والجهد ، والانكماش والجد . . متى تنفع ؟ لكنه من القسمة أيضا ما ظهر

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r1.claim: “My remembrance” can mean the Quran specifically, as “My Reminder,” or God's guidance generally, which reminds people of Him and calls them to Him.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r1.anchor: The remembrance of Me can refer to the Quran in particular

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r2.claim: A miserable life can mean a constricted life, especially spiritually.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r2.anchor: A miserable life is a life that is constricted

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is a worldly life focused on possessions and fear of losing them, contrasted with believers' hope in the Hereafter and life blessed by faith.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r3.anchor: Or, it may refer to a life in which one is merely given to the things of the world and lives in a state where he is fearful of their being taken away from him

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r4.speaker: al-Zamakhsharī
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī contrasts this miserable life with the believer's good life described in 16:97.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r4.anchor: Juxtaposing such people with the believers, al-Zamakhsharī calls attention to 16:97

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r5.claim: Afterlife blindness can occur despite earthly physical sight; it directly reflects spiritual blindness in this life.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r5.anchor: Some people are said to be raised blind on the Last Day and in the Hereafter, even though they could see with their physical sight while alive on earth

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r6.claim: Alternatively, those spiritually blind in this life will see the realities they rejected with clarity in the next life.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r6.anchor: From another perspective, those who were spiritually blind in this life will come to

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r1.claim: Turning away from God's reminder means rejecting it, refusing to respond, and failing to take heed and desist from continuing to oppose God's command.
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r1.anchor: ولم يتعظ به فينزجر عما هو عليه مقيم من خلافه أمر ربه

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r2.claim: Al-Tabari explains maʿīsha ḍankan as a constricted, difficult livelihood.
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r2.anchor: والضنك من المنازل والأماكن والمعايش: الشديد

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r3.claim: The form ḍank stays the same for masculine and feminine, singular, dual, and plural.
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r3.anchor: وعيش ضنك: الذكر والأنثى والواحد والاثنان والجمع بلفظ واحد

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r4.speaker: عنترة
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r4.claim: ʿAntara's verse uses ḍank for a cramped dwelling, illustrating the word's sense of narrowness.
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r4.anchor: ومنه قول عنترة: [البحر الكامل] وإن نزلوا بضنك أنزل

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the constricted livelihood as misery.
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] يقول: الشقاء

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses ḍank as narrow or constricted.

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: الضنك: الضيق

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r8.claim: Al-Hasan locates the disbelievers' constricted livelihood in Hell.
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r8.anchor: عن عوف، عن الحسن، في قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: في جهنم

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says the constricted livelihood is in Hell and consists of fiery thorn, zaqqum, and ghislin; al-ḍarīʿ is thorn from fire.
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r9.anchor: قال: ومعيشة ضنكا في النار شوك من نار وزقوم وغسلين، والضريع: شوك من نار

TAB-FULL:v16p193/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd rejects a worldly or grave meaning: livelihood and life are only in the afterlife, as he reads 89:24 to mean my livelihood.
TAB-FULL:v16p193/r10.anchor: وليس في القبر ولا في الدنيا معيشة، ما المعيشة والحياة إلا في الآخرة، وقرأ قول الله عز وجل: {يا ليتني قدمت لحياتي} [الفجر: 24]

TAB-FULL:v16p194/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r1.claim: Qatada also locates the constricted livelihood in the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: في النار

TAB-FULL:v16p194/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r2.claim: Another view locates the constricted livelihood in worldly life: even broad earnings are cramped when they are unlawful.
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى بذلك: فإن له معيشة في الدنيا حراما. قال: ووصف الله جل وعز معيشتهم بالضنك

TAB-FULL:v16p194/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r3.claim: ʿIkrima identifies it as the livelihood God has expanded for someone through unlawful means.
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: هي المعيشة التي أوسع الله عليه من الحرام

TAB-FULL:v16p194/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r4.speaker: قيس بن أبي حازم
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r4.claim: Qays ibn Abi Hazim calls it provision obtained through disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r4.anchor: عن قيس بن أبي حازم، في قول الله: {معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: رزقا في معصيته

TAB-FULL:v16p194/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak describes it as ill-gotten earnings, evil work, and bad provision.
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: العمل الخبيث، والرزق السيئ

TAB-FULL:v16p194/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r6.claim: Another worldly-life explanation says abundant wealth still feels constricted when spent amid denial that God will replace it, despair of His favor, and suspicion of Him.
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون ممن قال عنى أن لهؤلاء القوم المعيشة الضنك في الدنيا، إنما قيل لها ضنك وإن كانت واسعة

TAB-FULL:v16p194/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says wealth of any amount brings no good if its recipient does not fear God in its use; this is constricted livelihood, as bad expectations of God distress even the wealthy.
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ومن أعرض عن ذكري، فإن له معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] يقول: كل مال أعطيته عبدا من عبادي قل أو كثر

TAB-FULL:v16p194/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r8.claim: A further view identifies the constricted livelihood as the intermediate state and the punishment of the grave.
TAB-FULL:v16p194/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى بذلك: أن ذلك لهم في البرزخ، وهو عذاب القبر

TAB-FULL:v16p197/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri identifies the constricted livelihood as punishment in the grave.
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r1.anchor: عن النعمان بن أبي عياش، عن أبي سعيد الخدري، قال في قول الله: {معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: عذاب القبر

TAB-FULL:v16p197/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r2.claim: In another report Abu Saʿid says the grave is squeezed around the person until his ribs shift.
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r2.anchor: عن أبي حازم، عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي سعيد الخدري {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: يضيق عليه قبره حتى تختلف أضلاعه

TAB-FULL:v16p197/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r3.claim: Abu Saʿid says a disbeliever is tormented in the grave by ninety-nine dragons until resurrection; one dragon's breath would prevent crops growing on earth.
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد، أنه كان يقول: المعيشة الضنك: عذاب القبر، إنه يسلط على الكافر في قبره تسعة وتسعون تنينا تنهشه

TAB-FULL:v16p197/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra says the disbeliever's grave is closed in on him until his ribs shift; this is the constricted livelihood.
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: يطبق على الكافر قبره حتى تختلف فيه أضلاعه، وهي المعيشة الضنك

TAB-FULL:v16p197/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r5.speaker: أبو صالح، السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r5.claim: Abu Salih and al-Suddi identify the constricted livelihood as punishment in the grave.
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r5.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، عن أبي صالح، والسدي، في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: عذاب القبر

TAB-FULL:v16p197/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r6.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r6.claim: Abdullah also glosses the constricted livelihood as punishment in the grave.
TAB-FULL:v16p197/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مخارق، عن أبيه، عن عبد الله

TAB-FULL:v16p198/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r1.claim: A further report from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri identifies the constricted livelihood as grave punishment.
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r1.anchor: عن النعمان بن أبي عياش، عن أبي سعيد الخدري {معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] قال: عذاب القبر

TAB-FULL:v16p198/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r2.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the interpretation that the constricted livelihood is punishment in the grave.
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r2.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: هو عذاب القبر

TAB-FULL:v16p198/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r3.claim: The Prophet explains the constricted livelihood as the unbeliever's grave punishment: ninety-nine dragons, each a snake with seven heads, sting and scratch him until resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

TAB-FULL:v16p198/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r4.claim: The mention in 20:127 that the afterlife punishment is more severe establishes that the constricted livelihood precedes it, so it cannot itself be afterlife punishment.
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r4.anchor: ولعذاب الآخرة أشد وأبقى} [طه: 127] فكان معلوما بذلك أن المعيشة الضنك التي جعلها الله لهم قبل عذاب الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v16p198/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r5.claim: Because many unbelievers enjoy broader worldly lives than many obedient believers, the constricted livelihood cannot refer to worldly life; with the afterlife excluded, the grave remains.
TAB-FULL:v16p198/r5.anchor: وفي وجودنا كثيرا منهم أوسع معيشة من كثير من المقبلين على ذكر الله تبارك وتعالى، القانتين له المؤمنين

TAB-FULL:v16p201/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r1.claim: Abu Salih interprets being gathered blind as having no argument.
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r1.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، عن أبي صالح، في قوله: {ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى} [طه: 124] قال: ليس له حجة

TAB-FULL:v16p201/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r2.claim: Mujahid also takes the blindness to mean blindness to the proof or argument.
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى} [طه: 124] قال: عن الحجة

TAB-FULL:v16p201/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r3.claim: Another reported view is that the person will be blind in physical sight.

TAB-FULL:v16p201/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r4.claim: Al-Tabari reads the wording generally: the person is blind both to argument and to seeing things, since the verse does not specify one sense.
TAB-FULL:v16p201/r4.anchor: وهو أنه يحشر أعمى عن الحجة ورؤية الشيء كما أخبر جل ثناؤه، فعم ولم يخصص

SULAMI:v1p453#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r1.claim: Turning away from remembrance darkens one’s time and unsettles one’s provision.
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r1.anchor: قال : لا يعرض أحد عن ذكر ربه إلا أظلم عليه وقته ،

SULAMI:v1p453#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r2.claim: If people truly knew God, they would not turn away; He who turns away is returned to the kinds and colors suited to him.
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r2.anchor: وقال جعفر في هذه الآية : لو عرفوني ما أعرضوا عني

SULAMI:v1p453#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r3.claim: What they turned from was their own remembrance, not God’s true remembrance; those who truly remember Him cannot turn away from Him or turn to another.
SULAMI:v1p453#3/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي : ما كان ذلك ذكري حتى أعرضوا عنه

TABATABAI:20:124/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:124/r1.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:20:124/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib defines ʿaysh as life specific to animals, narrower than life said of animals, God, and angels; maʿīsha derives from what sustains life.
TABATABAI:20:124/r1.anchor: قال الراغب العيش الحياة المختصة بالحيوان وهو أخص من الحياة لأن الحياة يقال في الحيوان

TABATABAI:20:124/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:124/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:124/r2.claim: Ḍank means narrowness or constriction and has the same form for masculine and feminine; it originally is the verbal noun of ḍanka, “to become narrow.”
TABATABAI:20:124/r2.anchor: والضنك هو الضيق من كل شيء ويستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث

TABATABAI:20:124/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:124/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:124/r3.claim: Instead of saying “whoever does not follow My guidance,” the verse says “turns away from My remembrance,” identifying the cause of constricted life and blindness and preparing for the later mention of God's leaving the forgetful.
TABATABAI:20:124/r3.anchor: ليشير به إلى علة الحكم لأن نسيانه تعالى والإعراض عن ذكره هو السبب

TABATABAI:20:126/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:126/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:126/r1.claim: “My remembrance” may mean the act of remembering God, the Qurʾān or all revealed books, or the true call, which is called remembrance because following it entails remembering God.
TABATABAI:20:126/r1.anchor: فقوله { ذكري } من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله أو القرآن أو مطلق الكتب السماوية

TABATABAI:20:126/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:126/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:126/r2.claim: The forgetful person becomes attached to worldly life as the sole goal. No amount of livelihood satisfies him; desire keeps extending, leaving him distressed and anxious about loss, illness, envy, failure, and separation.
TABATABAI:20:126/r2.anchor: من نسي ربه وانقطع عن ذكره لم يبق له إلا أن يتعلق بالدنيا ويجعلها مطلوبه الوحيد

TABATABAI:20:126/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:126/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:126/r3.claim: Someone who remembers God knows of enduring life, dominion, honor, and joy with God; worldly life is temporary, so even modest provision can satisfy the believer.
TABATABAI:20:126/r3.anchor: ولو أنه عرف مقام ربه ذاكرا غير ناس أيقن أن له حياة عند ربه لا يخالطها موت

TABATABAI:20:126/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:126/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:126/r4.claim: Some identify the constricted life with grave torment and barzakh hardship because many who turn away from God prosper materially; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects comparing rich and poor, since the Qurʾān compares the believer's life with the forgetful unbeliever's.
TABATABAI:20:126/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمعيشة الضنك عذاب القبر وشقاء الحياة البرزخية

TABATABAI:20:126/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:126/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:126/r5.claim: Grave torment can be one instance of constricted life if the first clause describes their worldly condition and the resurrection clause their afterlife condition.
TABATABAI:20:126/r5.anchor: نعم عذاب القبر من مصاديق المعيشة الضنك بناء على كون قوله { فإن له معيشة ضنكا }

TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r1.claim: The grave may exemplify constricted life when the verse's first clause covers earthly life and the resurrection clause covers the afterlife, with the barzakh as an appendage of worldly life.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r1.anchor: لبيان حالهم في الآخرة والبرزخ من أذناب الدنيا

TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r2.claim: Another view makes constricted life the punishment of Hell and takes the blindness clause as the period before entry; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī objects that the first clause is unrestricted while the second specifies Judgment Day.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r2.anchor: عذاب النار يوم القيامة، وبقوله { ونحشره } الخ، ما قبل دخول النار

TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r3.claim: Being gathered blind means being unable to find the path to one's happiness, namely Paradise, as the next two verses show.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#2/r3.anchor: أي بحيث لا يهتدي إلى ما فيه سعادته وهو الجنة والدليل على ذلك ما يأتي في الآيتين التاليتين

TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r1.claim: Reports applying “whoever follows My guidance” and “My remembrance” to the wilāya of the Prophet's household are instances of Qurʾānic application (jary), not lexical interpretation.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r1.anchor: وقع فيها تطبيق قوله تعالى { فمن اتبع هداي } وقوله { عن ذكري } على ولاية أهل البيت

TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو سعيد الخدري والسدي
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r4.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports the view that constricted life means grave punishment, attributing it to Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and al-Suddī.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وأبي سعيد الخدري والسدي

TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r5.claim: The grave-punishment interpretation is also transmitted as a Prophetic report from Abū Hurayra.

TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r6.claim: In al-Kāfī, Abū Baṣīr reports from Abū ʿAbd Allāh that a healthy, affluent person who dies without performing pilgrimage is among those gathered blind; the Imam explains that God blinded him from the path of truth. Similar reports appear in al-Qummī and al-Ṣadūq.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r6.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال سمعت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول من مات وهو صحيح موسر لم يحج

TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r7.claim: This report specifies blindness as being deprived of the path of truth, salvation, and happiness, supporting the verse's interpretation as loss of guidance to felicity.
TABATABAI:20:115-126#6/r7.anchor: والرواية في تخصيصها عمى يوم القيامة بطريق الحق وهو طريق النجاة والسعادة تؤيد ما تقدم

TABRISI:20:124/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r3.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
TABRISI:20:124/r3.claim: In a noncanonical reading, Aban ibn Taghlib reads the gathering verb in the jussive.
TABRISI:20:124/r3.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة أبان بن تغلب ونحشره بالجزم

TABRISI:20:124/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124/r4.claim: The jussive reading coordinates the verb with the syntactic position of the conditional answer, which is jussive.
TABRISI:20:124/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ نحشره فإنه عطفه على موضع قوله

TABRISI:20:124/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124/r6.claim: Ḍank means a constricted, difficult state; as a verbal noun, it does not take dual, plural, or feminine forms.
TABRISI:20:124/r6.anchor: والضنك الضيق الصعب يقال منزل ضنك وعيش ضنك لا يثنى ولا يجمع ولا يؤنث

TABRISI:20:124#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124#2/r12.claim: Turning away from God’s remembrance means turning away from the Qur’an and the proofs God revealed to His servants, refusing to consider them.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r12.anchor: أي ومن أعرض عن القرآن وعن الدلائل التي أنزلها الله تعالى لعباده وصدف عنها ولم ينظر فيها

TABRISI:20:124#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، الجبائي
TABRISI:20:124#2/r13.claim: They explain the constricted livelihood as a punishment: God may restrict provision, or make even ample wealth oppressive through hoarding and endless desire for more.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r13.anchor: أي عيشا ضيقا عن مجاهد وقتادة والجبائي

TABRISI:20:124#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود، أبو سعيد الخدري، أبو هريرة
TABRISI:20:124#2/r14.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud and Abu Sa‘id explain the constricted life as punishment in the grave; Abu Hurayra transmits this interpretation as a Prophetic report.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r14.anchor: هو عذاب القبر عن ابن مسعود وأبي سعيد الخدري والسدي

TABRISI:20:124#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r15.speaker: الحسن، ابن زيد
TABRISI:20:124#2/r15.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd take it as the food of hell, including ḍarīʿ and zaqqūm, even if the person had worldly abundance.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r15.anchor: وقيل: هو طعام الضريع والزقوم في جهنم لأن ماله إليها وإن كان في سعة من الدنيا عن الحسن وابن زيد

TABRISI:20:124#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:124#2/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person spends in a troubled way, without confidence that God will replace what is spent.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r16.anchor: وقيل: معناه أن يكون عيشه منغصا بأن ينفق إنفاق من لا يوقن بالخلف عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:20:124#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r17.speaker: عكرمة، الضحاك
TABRISI:20:124#2/r17.claim: Ikrima and al-Dahhak interpret it as unlawful earnings in this world that lead to hell.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r17.anchor: وقيل: هو الحرام في الدنيا الذي يؤدي إلى النار عن عكرمة والضحاك

TABRISI:20:124#2/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r18.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:20:124#2/r18.claim: Abu Muslim understands it as worldly life being short and clouded by troubles; only life in Paradise is truly pleasant.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r18.anchor: وقيل: عيشا ضيقا في الدنيا لقصرها وسائر ما يشوبها ويكدرها وإنما العيش الرغد في الجنة عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:20:124-125/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124-125/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:124-125/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the blindness at resurrection literally as blindness of sight.
TABRISI:20:124-125/r1.anchor: أي أعمى البصر عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:20:124-125/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124-125/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:20:124-125/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets the blindness as having no argument or proof to guide the person.
TABRISI:20:124-125/r2.anchor: وقيل: أعمى عن الحجة عن مجاهد

TABRISI:20:124-125/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124-125/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124-125/r3.claim: The literal blindness of sight is preferable because it is the apparent meaning and the next verse says the person had previously been seeing.
TABRISI:20:124-125/r3.anchor: والأول هو الوجه لأنه الظاهر ولا مانع منه

TABRISI:20:124-125/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124-125/r4.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:20:124-125/r4.claim: Al-Farra says the person leaves the grave seeing, then becomes blind during the gathering.
TABRISI:20:124-125/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: يقال إنه يخرج من قبره بصيرا فيعمى في حشره

TABRISI:20:124-125/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124-125/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:20:124-125/r5.claim: Mu‘awiya ibn ‘Ammar reports that Imam al-Sadiq applies the verse to a wealthy man who failed to perform pilgrimage, explaining that God blinded him to the path of truth.
TABRISI:20:124-125/r5.anchor: روى معاوية بن عمار قال سألت أبا عبد الله ع

TABRISI:20:124-125/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124-125/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124-125/r6.claim: The report aligns with interpreting blindness as being unable to find any path of good.
TABRISI:20:124-125/r6.anchor: فهذا يطابق قول من قال إن المعنى في الآية أعمى عن جهات الخير

FARRA:v2p194/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p194/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p194/r8.claim: He is blind to the proof; alternatively, he leaves the grave sighted and becomes blind during the gathering.
FARRA:v2p194/r8.anchor: أعمى عن الحجة، ويقال: إنه يخرج من قبره بصيرا فيعمى في حشره.

THALABI:v6p264/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p264/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p264/r9.claim: God’s remembrance here means the Qur’an; turning away means neither believing nor following it.
THALABI:v6p264/r9.anchor: ومن أعرض عن ذكري يعني عن القرآن فلم يؤمن به ولم يتبعه

THALABI:v6p264/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p264/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p264/r10.claim: Ḍank means constricted or narrow, as in a narrow dwelling or constricted life.
THALABI:v6p264/r10.anchor: ضيقا يقال: منزل ضنك وعيش ضنك

THALABI:v6p264/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p264/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p264/r11.claim: The form ḍank is used alike for masculine and feminine, singular, dual, and plural.
THALABI:v6p264/r11.anchor: يستوي فيه الذكر والأنثى والواحد والاثنان والجمع

THALABI:v6p264/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p264/r12.speaker: عنترة
THALABI:v6p264/r12.claim: Antarah’s verse uses ḍank to describe a narrow place where a group settles.
THALABI:v6p264/r12.anchor: قال عنترة: وإذا هم نزلوا بضنك فانزل

THALABI:v6p265/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v6p265/r1.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says the constricted life is the punishment of the grave.
THALABI:v6p265/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

THALABI:v6p265/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p265/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the constricted life as misery.
THALABI:v6p265/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الشقاء، مجاهد: الضيق، الحسن وابن زيد

THALABI:v6p265/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p265/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets the constricted life as narrowness.
THALABI:v6p265/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الشقاء، مجاهد: الضيق، الحسن وابن زيد

THALABI:v6p265/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r4.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد
THALABI:v6p265/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd identify it with the foods zaqqum, ghislin, and dari.
THALABI:v6p265/r4.anchor: الحسن وابن زيد: الزقوم والغسلين والضريع، قتادة: يعني في النار

THALABI:v6p265/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p265/r5.claim: Qatada says the constricted life is in the Fire.
THALABI:v6p265/r5.anchor: الضريع، قتادة: يعني في النار، عكرمة: الحرام

THALABI:v6p265/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r6.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p265/r6.claim: Ikrima interprets it as unlawful livelihood.
THALABI:v6p265/r6.anchor: يعني في النار، عكرمة: الحرام، قيس بن أبي حازم: الرزق

THALABI:v6p265/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r7.speaker: قيس بن أبي حازم
THALABI:v6p265/r7.claim: Qays ibn Abi Hazim says it is provision gained through disobedience.
THALABI:v6p265/r7.anchor: عكرمة: الحرام، قيس بن أبي حازم: الرزق في المعصية

THALABI:v6p265/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r8.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v6p265/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets it as ill-gotten earnings.
THALABI:v6p265/r8.anchor: قيس بن أبي حازم: الرزق في المعصية، الضحاك: الكسب الخبيث

THALABI:v6p265/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r9.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p265/r9.claim: Atiyya from Ibn Abbas says wealth brings no good and remains constricted when its recipient does not fear God in using it; even the wealthy disbeliever is troubled by distrust and denial.
THALABI:v6p265/r9.anchor: عطية عن ابن عباس يقول: كل مال أعطيته عبدا من عبادي قل أو كثر لا يتقيني فيه فلا خير فيه

THALABI:v6p265/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v6p265/r10.claim: Abu Saeed al-Khudri says the grave is squeezed until the ribs cross and ninety-nine seven-headed dragons torment the deceased until resurrection.
THALABI:v6p265/r10.anchor: أبو سعيد الخدري: يضيق عليه قبره حتى تختلف أضلاعه ويسلط عليه في قبره تسعة وتسعون تنينا

THALABI:v6p265/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r11.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p265/r11.claim: Muqatil says it is an evil life because it is spent in disobedience to God.
THALABI:v6p265/r11.anchor: مقاتل: معيشة سوء لأنها في معاصي الله. سعيد بن جبير: سلبه القناعة

THALABI:v6p265/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v6p265/r12.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the person loses contentment and is never satisfied.
THALABI:v6p265/r12.anchor: مقاتل: معيشة سوء لأنها في معاصي الله. سعيد بن جبير: سلبه القناعة حتى لا يشبع

THALABI:v6p265/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p265/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the blindness at resurrection literally as blindness of sight.
THALABI:v6p265/r13.anchor: ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى قال ابن عباس: أعمى البصر، مجاهد: أعمى عن الحجة

THALABI:v6p265/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r14.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p265/r14.claim: Mujahid interprets the blindness as being without an argument or proof.
THALABI:v6p265/r14.anchor: ونحشره يوم القيامة أعمى قال ابن عباس: أعمى البصر، مجاهد: أعمى عن الحجة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses God's reminder as His admonition.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets it as the Qurʾān, which the person neither believes nor follows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (عن القرآن فلم يؤمن به ولم يتبعه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r3.claim: Ḍank means constriction and distress; anything constricted can be called ḍank, as in a constricted house or life, and the word is used for constricted living.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r3.anchor: الضنك أصله في اللغة: الضيق والشدة، وكل ما ضاق فهو ضنك يقال: منزل ضنك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda cites ʿAntara's verse about death appearing when people settle in a constricted dwelling to attest the sense of ḍank.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r4.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة قول عنترة (¬7): إن المنية لو تمثل مثلت ... مثلي إذا نزلوا بضنك المنزل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r5.claim: A large-bodied woman is called ḍanāk because her skin is tight over her flesh; ḍank is originally a verbal noun then used adjectivally, explaining the feminine form maʿīshatan ḍankā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r5.anchor: ومنه قيل للمرأة الضخمة الكثيرة اللحم: ضناك؛ لأن جلدها قد ضاق بلحمها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r6.speaker: النبي، أبو هريرة، أبو سعيد الخدري، ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r6.claim: The most common exegetical view, attributed to the Prophet and to Abū Hurayra, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, and Ibn Masʿūd, is that the constricted life is punishment in the grave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r6.anchor: وأكثر ما جاء في التفسير المعيشة الضنك: (أنه عذاب القبر) عن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-، وعن أبي هريرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r7.speaker: الحسن، الكلبي، ابن زيد، قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Kalbī, Ibn Zayd, and Qatāda interpret the constricted life as punishment in the Fire, including food of zaqqūm, ghislīn, and ḍarīʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن، والكلبي، وابن زيد، وقتادة: (هو عذاب النار، وأكل الزقوم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r8.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, Ibn ʿAbbās specifies the punishment of the grave as its squeeze until the ribs are displaced.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يريد: ضغطة القبر حتى تختلف أضلاعه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r9.claim: In al-Wālibī's report, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as the wretched or miserable person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p550/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يريد: ضغطة القبر حتى تختلف أضلاعه) (¬1). وقال في رواية الوالبي: (الشقي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r1.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r1.claim: One interpretation is that the person will be blind in his eyesight.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that he will be blind to proof or argument.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains that the person has no proof to guide him, or has proof but is blinded to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (وتأويله أنه لا حجة له يهتدي إليها، أن له حجة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r4.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r4.claim: Another scholar says that when blindness is unqualified, its apparent sense is blindness of sight; the following passage supports this view, though the excerpt breaks off before completing the evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p552/r4.anchor: وقال غيره: (العمى إذا أطلق كان الظاهر عمى البصر)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r2.claim: The hereafter's punishment is more awful and greater than the grave punishment just mentioned; this supports reading the constricted life as punishment of the grave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r2.anchor: وهذا يدلس على أن المراد بقوله: {معيشة ضنكا}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r1.claim: God's remembrance here is His admonition, the Qur'an.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r1.anchor: { من أعرض عن ذكري } موعظتي، وهي القرآن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r2.claim: The constricted life means narrowness in Hell.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r2.anchor: { فإن له معيشة ضنكا } ضيقى. يعني: في جهنم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r3.claim: Another view is that the constricted life means punishment in the grave.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:124-125/r4.claim: God will resurrect the person blind in sight.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r6.claim: Turning away from God’s reminder means not following His guidance and not believing.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r7.claim: The Prophet explains the constricted life as punishment in the grave.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p285#2/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] : عذاب القبر "

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the constricted life means punishment in the grave.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r1.anchor: عن القاسم بن عبد الرحمن، عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: {معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] : عذاب القبر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r2.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri says it is grave punishment that presses upon a person until his ribs shift.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r2.anchor: عن النعمان بن أبي عياش، عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: {معيشة ضنكا} [طه: 124] : عذاب القبر، يلتئم على صاحبه حتى تختلف أضلاعه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r3.speaker: أبو القاسم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r3.claim: Abu al-Qasim describes the believer’s grave: charity, Quran recitation, and prayer protect him; he answers the angel’s questions and is shown his place in Paradise, while the disbeliever has no such protection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p286/r3.anchor:
ألا أحدثكم ما حدثني به خليلي أبو القاسم؟ قال: قلت: بلى.
قال: فإنه حدثنا أن الرجل المؤمن إذا وضع في قبره فانصرف الناس،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r1.speaker: أبو القاسم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r1.claim: The grave report continues: the disbeliever is struck, cries out so loudly that humans and jinn hear, and is laid on two boards of fire as his grave contracts around him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r1.anchor: ضربة يضج منها ضجة يسمعها من على الأرض إلى الثقلين، وينادي مناد: أن افرشوه لوحين من نار،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r2.claim: Being raised blind means being without an argument, as in 23:117, which says one who invokes another god has no proof.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r2.anchor:
يعني عن حجته كقوله:
{ومن يدع مع الله إلها آخر لا برهان له به} [المؤمنون: 117] لا حجة له به.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r13.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r13.claim: Turning away from God’s remembrance is explained as denying God, disapproving of His way, or refusing to heed His admonitions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r13.anchor: “Allah’ı anmaktan yüz çevirme”, Allah’ı inkâr etme, O’nun gösterdiği yolu beğenmeme, öğütlerine kulak asmama gibi mânalarla açıklanmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r14.speaker: ilk dönem müfessirleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r14.claim: One reported view locates the constricted life of 20:124 in the stage of life in the grave.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r14.anchor: ilk dönem müfessirlerinden farklı rivayet ve yorumlar nakledilmiştir. Burada sözü edilen sıkıntılı yaşantının kabir hayatı aşamasıyla ilgili olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r15.speaker: ilk dönem müfessirleri
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r15.claim: Another reported view takes the constricted life as referring to hardships in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r15.anchor: âhirette yaşanacak sıkıntılara işaret edildiği rivayetlerinin yanı sıra dünya hayatındaki sıkıntılar anlamına ağırlık veren rivayet ve izahlar da vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r16.claim: The author gives weight to a worldly reading: even material abundance cannot spare such people the distress of disbelief, misguided aims and unlawful earnings, or the pain of lacking the joy of seeking God’s approval.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r16.anchor: Dünya hayatındaki sıkıntı, bu tür kimselerin maddî açıdan bolluk içinde olsalar bile, inançsızlığın, yanlış hedeflere yönelmenin, haram yollardan kazanmanın verdiği psikolojik baskı altında

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r17.claim: Those who reject God and the afterlife also live within a materially and spiritually narrower conception of life than believers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:115/r17.anchor: Allah’a ve âhirete inanmayanların, inananlara göre çok daha dar bir maddî-mânevî alan tasavvuru

NAHHAS:v3p59/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p59/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p59/r1.claim: The constricted life is the punishment of the grave.

ITQAN:v1p295#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r1.claim: It is disliked to make reciting the Qur'an a means of earning a livelihood; a report warns against reciting it to ask people for money.
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r1.anchor: يكره اتخاذ القرآن معيشة يتكسب بها وأخرج الآجري من حديث عمران بن الحصين مرفوعا

ITQAN:v1p295#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r2.claim: ʿImrān b. Ḥuṣayn reports the Prophet warning that people will recite the Qur'an while asking people for payment through it; no grading is stated.
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r2.anchor: من قرأ القرآن فليسأل الله به فإنه سيأتي قوم يقرؤون القرآن يسألون الناس به

ITQAN:v1p295#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r3.claim: Al-Bukhārī's Tārīkh al-Kabīr transmits with a صالح chain a report that one who recites the Qur'an before an unjust ruler to gain favor is cursed ten times per letter.
ITQAN:v1p295#3/r3.anchor: وروى البخاري في تاريخه الكبير بسند صالح حديث من قرأ القرآن عند ظالم ليرفع منه لعن بكل حرف عشر لعنات

ITQAN:v4p522/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p522/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p522/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a good-chain Prophetic explanation that the constricted life mentioned in the verse means the punishment of the grave.
ITQAN:v4p522/r2.anchor: وأخرج البزار بسند جيد عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ فإن له معيشة ضنكا ﴾ قال ( عذاب القبر )

ITQAN:v2p366/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p366/r8.speaker: غير مسمى
ITQAN:v2p366/r8.claim: The report defines ضنكا as severe narrowness or hardship and adduces an unnamed poet's description of a tight pass.
ITQAN:v2p366/r8.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ معيشة ضنكا ﴾ قال الضنك الضيق الشديد أما سمعت قول الشاعر

DAMGHANI:v1p332/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r11.claim: Blindness can mean lacking a proof: the resurrected person is blind to the argument for his punishment.
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r11.anchor: العمى عن الحجة قوله تعالى في سورة طه ونحشره يوم القيامة اعمى يعني عن الحجة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p303/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p303/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p303/r1.claim: The reported Qurʾānic senses of dhikr include monotheistic recognition of God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p303/r1.anchor: والسادس : التوحيد . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121/r2.claim: Al-aʿmā can mean blind to proof or evidence.

NASHR:v2p81/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p81/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the listed non-verse-final words on the routes that incline verse endings; for موسى he follows his usual between-vowels reading where imāla is transmitted.
NASHR:v2p81/r7.anchor: فإن أبا عمرو يفتح جميع ذلك من طريق المميلين له رءوس الآي لأنه ليس برأس آية

NASHR:v2p81/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r8.speaker: الأزرق عن ورش
NASHR:v2p81/r8.claim: Al-Azraq’s Warsh routes through Ibn Ghalbūn and others open these non-final forms; al-Taysīr and related routes read them between vowels because they are written with yāʾ, including فأما من طغى.
NASHR:v2p81/r8.anchor: والأزرق عن ورش يفتح جميعه أيضا من طريق أبي الحسن بن غلبون، وأبيه عبد المنعم ومكي

NASHR:v2p42/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p42/r5.speaker: أبو بكر
NASHR:v2p42/r5.claim: Abū Bakr uses imāla for both occurrences; Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb agree on the first, while Ibn Mihrān uniquely reports fatḥ from Rawḥ and al-Mubij uniquely reports imāla in two Ṭā Hā occurrences.
NASHR:v2p42/r5.anchor: فوافق على إمالتهما أبو بكر من جميع طرقه. ووافق على إمالة الأول أبو عمرو ويعقوب
